info.title: Revero Public API
info.description:
Create meetings, upload audio directly, follow authoritative operations and retrieve generated outputs. See the complete quickstart at https://docs.revero.no/welcome.

This is not a browser-callable surface: service credentials, bearer tokens and authenticated calls belong only in your backend. Browser code receives only the short-lived presigned upload request.

Replay a lost completion response with the SAME `Idempotency-Key`. After a terminal retryable failure, send a NEW `Idempotency-Key`; the old key still names the failed operation.

A new key while work is still outstanding is a `409`, as is one after `retryable: false`. `transcription_empty` (silent OR unintelligible audio) and `upload_unreadable` need new audio and a new meeting. `processing_not_entitled`, `output_profile_unavailable`, `organisation_key_unavailable` and `jurisdiction_unavailable` require an administrator or operator. Branch on `failure_code`.

Acquire a token from `/oauth/partner/token`. Every `/public/v1` error uses `{"code", "message"}`; branch on the stable `code`, never the message. OAuth token errors use the RFC 6749 error shape.

200.description: OAuth metadata for the Revero partner issuer.

post.summary: Exchange a client credential for an access token
post.description: Authenticate with HTTP Basic using the integration client ID and secret. The form must request the exact advertised resource and an explicit space-separated scope set. Client secrets must only be used by a backend.

200.description: A short-lived bearer token for the requested scopes.

400.description: The grant, resource, or scope is invalid.

503.description: The authorization server cannot issue a token.

get.description:
List the output profiles your organisation may name in `output_profiles`.

Resolved for the calling organisation, not the platform catalogue: a
document Revero restricts to selected organisations is absent here for
everyone else, and `POST /meetings` refuses exactly what this omits. Each
entry's `version` is what a meeting created now would pin.

200.description: The documents this organisation may ask a meeting to produce.

401.description: `invalid_token` — the bearer token is missing, expired, revoked, or belongs to a client whose organisation is suspended or no longer entitled to the Public API. Obtain a new token; if that also fails, an administrator must act.

403.description: `insufficient_scope` — the token is valid but was not issued with the scope this route requires. Request the scope at token exchange.

post.description: Create a meeting, idempotent within the OAuth client by external_id.

201.description: A newly created meeting and its declared outputs.

422.description: `unknown_output_profile` — an `output_profiles` entry names a document this release does not offer; the message lists the offending keys and the valid ones, and `GET /output-profiles` lists what your organisation may ask for. `validation_error` — any other malformed body.

401.description: `invalid_token` — the bearer token is missing, expired, revoked, or belongs to a client whose organisation is suspended or no longer entitled to the Public API. Obtain a new token; if that also fails, an administrator must act.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, or `output_profile_unavailable` — a requested output profile's template is not available to this organisation. The key is valid; the grant is missing, and only an administrator can add one. Retrying will not change the answer. Or `transcription_minutes_used_up` — the organisation has used the transcription minutes of its plan for this period. A replay of a meeting already created is not refused. New minutes come with the next period, or when an administrator adds them.

200.description: Idempotent replay — a meeting with this `external_id` already existed and the request matches it. The same resource is returned; nothing was created.

409.description: `external_id_conflict` — this `external_id` already identifies a different request (another language, or another set of output profiles). Use a new `external_id`; the first request's `locked_context` is never restated.

503.description: `processing_unavailable` — Revero cannot process content in this environment yet. Platform-wide, identical for every organisation here, and changed by neither you nor a Revero administrator. Not a retry you can win; contact Revero.

get.description: Read one meeting owned by the calling OAuth client.

200.description: The meeting, recording metadata and declared outputs.

401.description: `invalid_token` — the bearer token is missing, expired, revoked, or belongs to a client whose organisation is suspended or no longer entitled to the Public API. Obtain a new token; if that also fails, an administrator must act.

403.description: `insufficient_scope` — the token is valid but was not issued with the scope this route requires. Request the scope at token exchange.

404.description: `meeting_not_found` — no meeting with this id belongs to the calling integration client. An id belonging to another client or another organisation is a 404, not a 403.

503.description: `processing_unavailable` — the stored context cannot be read in this environment. See `POST /meetings`: platform-wide, not a setting on your organisation.

post.description: Create a recording and return a one-hour direct-upload request.

201.description: A recording resource and its short-lived direct-upload instruction.

401.description: `invalid_token` — the bearer token is missing, expired, revoked, or belongs to a client whose organisation is suspended or no longer entitled to the Public API. Obtain a new token; if that also fails, an administrator must act.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`, or `transcription_minutes_used_up` — the organisation has used the transcription minutes of its plan for this period. New minutes come with the next period, or when an administrator adds them.

409.description: `meeting_not_accepting_uploads` — this meeting has already moved past the upload stage.

415.description: `unsupported_audio_type` — the declared `content_type` is not an audio type Revero accepts.

post.description: Verify the uploaded object and accept transcription asynchronously.

202.description: The authoritative operation accepted for asynchronous processing.

401.description: `invalid_token` — the bearer token is missing, expired, revoked, or belongs to a client whose organisation is suspended or no longer entitled to the Public API. Obtain a new token; if that also fails, an administrator must act.

403.description: `insufficient_scope` — the token is valid but was not issued with the scope this route requires. Request the scope at token exchange.

404.description: `recording_not_found` — no recording with this id belongs to the calling integration client.

409.description: One of: `recording_already_completed` (this recording was completed under a different Idempotency-Key), `meeting_already_processing` (a DIFFERENT recording for this meeting is already being processed — one meeting carries one recording, so poll that operation or create a new meeting), `upload_expired` (the presigned grant lapsed — prepare a new recording), `upload_not_found` (no object at the expected location: the browser upload did not finish), `empty_upload` (the object is zero bytes), or `uploaded_content_type_mismatch` (the stored type differs from the one declared).

413.description: `upload_too_large` — the object exceeds the maximum upload size.

502.description: `dispatch_failed` — the command was accepted and stored, but processing could not be started. Retry with the SAME `Idempotency-Key`; the replay re-dispatches it rather than creating a second operation.

post.summary: Receive a terminal operation or output event
post.description: Revero delivers terminal events at least once and without ordering guarantees, following Standard Webhooks (standardwebhooks.com). Verify `webhook-signature` against the exact request bytes with your `whsec_` secret before decoding this body, deduplicate on `webhook-id`, return a 2xx response quickly, and reconcile through the authenticated links. Revero retries every other response, and timeouts, for about three days. A 410 disables the endpoint. Redirects are not followed.

parameters.description: The stable event ID. The same on every retry.

schema.title: Webhook-Id
schema.description: The stable event ID. The same on every retry.

parameters.name: webhook-id

parameters.description: When this attempt was sent, in Unix seconds.

schema.title: Webhook-Timestamp
schema.description: When this attempt was sent, in Unix seconds.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp

parameters.description: Space-separated `v1,<base64>` HMAC-SHA256 signatures over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`. Accept any matching `v1` during rotation.

schema.title: Webhook-Signature
schema.description: Space-separated `v1,<base64>` HMAC-SHA256 signatures over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`. Accept any matching `v1` during rotation.

parameters.name: webhook-signature

204.description: The receiver accepted the event for reconciliation.

422.description: The receiver rejected the event body. Revero retries it like any other failure, so answer 2xx for an event you will ignore.

410.description: The receiver is gone for good. Revero stops this delivery and disables the endpoint until an admin enables it again.

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description:
Your own identifier for this meeting. Creation is idempotent on it: re-sending an identical request returns the same meeting with 200 instead of 201. Re-using it for a DIFFERENT request (other documents, another language) is a 409 `external_id_conflict`.

One meeting carries ONE recording, so this identifier is what decides the shape of your own data model. A gathering captured in several sittings, such as a lunch break or a session resumed the next day, is several meetings with several `external_id`s, not several recordings under one. Completing a second recording for a meeting already being processed is a 409 `meeting_already_processing`.

language.title: Language
language.description: Spoken language, for transcription and generation.

output_profiles.title: Output Profiles
output_profiles.description: Which documents this meeting should produce, by stable profile key. Each becomes one output resource you fetch separately. The profile VERSION is pinned now: publishing a new version later never changes what this meeting produces. Defaults to the transcript alone.

locked_context.title: Locked Context
locked_context.description: Your authoritative facts about this meeting — a case number, participants, a date. Stored encrypted, returned as its own field, and never rewritten by generation: your system stays authoritative for legal and business facts. Captured ONCE, on the request that creates the meeting, so a later call with the same external_id cannot restate it under documents already generated from it. At most 16384 bytes serialized.

The aggregate: one meeting, its recordings and its declared documents.

command.description: Which command this receipt is for.

status.description: One of five coarse states. `queued` and `processing` mean work is outstanding; the other three are terminal and will not change.

phase.description: Which stage the work has reached. Informational, for showing progress — do not branch on it; branch on `status`.

failure_code.description: Why the operation failed, or null. A closed set of stable values — branch on this rather than on the HTTP status or the message.

retryable.title: Retryable
retryable.description: Whether re-sending could succeed at all. Null until the operation fails. False means a retry would fail identically, but the reason differs by `failure_code`, and only some need an administrator, so branch on the code rather than on this alone.

completed_at.title: Completed At
completed_at.description: When it reached a terminal state.

OperationRead.title: OperationRead
OperationRead.description:
The durable receipt for one accepted command — poll this.

After a dropped connection, a closed browser or a missed notification,
reading this resource is enough to learn what happened.

profile_version.description: Pinned when the meeting was created. A newer version published since then does not apply to this document.

schema_version.description: Version of the public payload shape used by `content` and `structured_data` for this output.

completed_at.title: Completed At

content.title: Content
content.description:
The document as CommonMark. Null unless `status` is `completed`.

Claims grounded in the meeting are wrapped in a `<cite>` element marking them as evidenced: `data-seg` names a transcript segment, `data-page` a page in a document you supplied, and an optional `data-src` says which source. The wrapped text is ordinary prose and reads correctly without the tags, so a renderer that does not want provenance should REMOVE the `<cite>` elements rather than escape them. Rendering this markdown raw shows the markup to your users.

Those numbers are OUR segment numbering and the `transcript` output does not carry it, so resolving a `data-seg` to a segment is not supported yet. Treat the tags as a signal that a sentence is grounded, not as a join key.

structured_data.title: Structured Data
structured_data.description: The same answer as machine-readable fields, when this profile declares them — `schema_version` says which shape. Null for profiles that produce prose only, and null unless `status` is `completed`.

OutputContentRead.title: OutputContentRead
OutputContentRead.description:
One output plus content when generation has completed.

Meeting polls return output metadata only. Fetch content one output at a
time after its status becomes ``completed``.

PresignedUpload.title: PresignedUpload
PresignedUpload.description:
A single-object upload grant. The only thing here safe to give a browser.

It carries no Revero credential and authorises writing one object, once,
until it expires. Never send your client secret or bearer token to browser
code.

PublicApiError.title: PublicApiError
PublicApiError.description:
One refusal, as a stable code plus prose a human reads.

Every `/public/v1` error uses this flat shape. The code is the stable
protocol; the message is explanatory prose and may be reworded.

PublicWebhookEnvelope.title: PublicWebhookEnvelope
PublicWebhookEnvelope.description:
A Standard Webhooks body: a terminal public resource state, signed and
delivered at least once. The event ID is the `webhook-id` header.

PublicWebhookEventType.title: PublicWebhookEventType
PublicWebhookEventType.description:
Every event that may leave an organisation over this surface.

The product contract ADR-0072 asked for, stated as a closed set. Terminal
only: there is no "started", no "progress" and no percentage, because a
partner reconciles from the authoritative GET and a notification only
accelerates that (ADR-0072, "Status and delivery").
